posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
Well, a few things that stick out to me.
1 - it's odd that these are all map events. Maybe that's just for your testing, but one would assume the time system applies to your entire game, not just one map, so they should be common events.
2 - it's also odd that you have things split into two separate events instead of combined into one. As a general rule, you don't want to have more parallel processes running than you need.
Speaking of:
3 - you should almost never have a parallel event running without a Wait command at the top or bottom. By default, parallel and autorun events run every frame, 60 times a second. That could well be the cause of your issue: the event is checking the time every frame and restarting the tint, so you never actually see it happen.

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
one additional comment:
the transfer command should be the last command of any event, unless the transfer stays within the same map - and even then it would be better.
all map events get deleted the second you leave the current map. and that includes the map event with the transfer.
most of the time the event processing sequence will continue the active event even on a map transfer, but only if everything runs in the same frame as the transfer command.
If there is any command that needs more time than that frame, then everything after it will never be processed, because in the next frame the event doesn't exist anymore.
so unless you know exactly what you're doing, you cannot guarantee that the commands after a transfer will be executed unless they are placed on the next map.

posts.author: caethyril
posts.body:
@Andar
- to clarify, on transfer to a different map:
A Parallel event will halt immediately, but
A non-Parallel event will run to completion.
Transfer Player uses a wait mode to prevent the interpreter from processing any more commands until the transfer is complete, including any transfer fade-in. (If the transfer is performed via script call, it's possible to omit setting the wait mode, which could cause odd behaviour like you describe.)
Spoiler:
technical explanation
When an event starts,
its commands are placed into the applicable event interpreter
; only the state of that interpreter determines when the event stops. A Parallel event's interpreter is a property of that Parallel event, and like you say, all events (including common events) are cleared on map transfer. By contrast, non-Parallel events run in the main interpreter, which remains intact on map transfer.
A simple test event:
◆Text：None, None, Window, Bottom
：    ：Transferring...
◆Transfer Player：Another Map (5,6)
◆Text：None, None, Window, Bottom
：    ：Transferred!
The "Transferred!" message shows only when the trigger is
not
set to Parallel.
(As always, plugins can change any aspect of the engine.)
Also, some commands (Erase Event and character-target commands) may behave unexpectedly if they originated from an event on a different map.
